title: 8 Best Conversational AI Platforms for Retail Banking (2026)
summary: 8 conversational AI platforms rated for retail banking on telephony ownership, latency, compliance, pricing, and omnichannel support.
body_markdown:
### TLDR


-


Regulated retail banks needing voice + chat + SMS: Plivo, the only platform combining owned telephony in 150+ countries with PCI DSS, SOC 2, and HIPAA compliance


-


Banks already running Twilio infrastructure: Twilio, but expect bolted-on AI architecture and higher per-minute costs


-


Developer teams building custom banking voice products: Vapi, API-only with maximum modularity


-


Community banks wanting fast, no-code deployment: Synthflow AI, low barrier but low ceiling


-


Pricing range: $0.004/participant-min (LiveKit audio-only) to ~$0.25/min all-in (Twilio)


Your retail bank fields thousands of calls a day about stolen cards, balance inquiries, and payment disputes. Most of those calls still hit a legacy IVR tree that frustrates callers into hanging up or waiting for a human agent.


According to[UnitelVoice's compilation of call handling research](https://www.unitelvoice.com/blog/fortune-500-phone-system-stats/) , 27% of customers abandoned calls due to IVR frustration, and 51% abandoned the company entirely after encountering an automated menu. That's revenue walking out the door on every call.


You're here because you want a conversational AI platform that can actually handle those calls. But most comparison articles treat "conversational AI" as a synonym for text chatbots and ignore the voice channel, which still carries the majority of retail banking customer interactions.


This article focuses on voice-capable platforms and rates them on the six factors retail banking procurement actually cares about: telephony ownership, latency, compliance depth, builder flexibility, omnichannel support, and post-deployment quality tooling.

## What Actually Matters for Retail Banking


Generic conversational AI comparisons miss what banking procurement actually demands. Here's what to check for on any platform you're evaluating:


1.


Telephony ownership. Does the vendor own its carrier network, or route through a third party? A rented network adds 50–150ms of latency and a second point of failure, which is a real problem when a call drops mid-fraud-report. Only Plivo and Twilio own their infrastructure. For banking, this is a procurement filter, not a preference.


2.


End-to-end latency. Ask for published, independently benchmarked numbers, not marketing claims. Anything above ~500ms starts to sound unnatural on calls about stolen cards or disputes. In one Tested Media benchmark of 500 production calls, Vapi measured 720ms median, Bland AI 850ms median, and ElevenLabs 1,424ms median. Every extra hop between the AI layer and telephony widens the gap.


3.


Full-stack compliance. PCI DSS, SOC 2, and GDPR (plus HIPAA where relevant) should be table stakes before evaluation even starts. But check whether certifications cover the entire call path (carrier, AI processing, recording, storage), or just parts of it stitched to a third-party carrier's separate audit.


4.


Both code and no-code access. Confirm non-technical teams (branch ops, compliance, contact center managers) can update agents without filing engineering tickets, while the platform still supports the complex logic (multi-step ID verification, conditional routing) that pure no-code tools can't handle.


5.


Omnichannel continuity. Ask whether voice, SMS, and messaging share context on one system, or run as separate products with separate configs. A customer who calls, gets a text confirmation, then follows up on WhatsApp shouldn't have to repeat themselves.


6.


Post-launch quality tooling. Most failures show up at week four, not launch day, when an agent handles the easy 88% fine and stumbles on the hard 12%. Look for built-in tools to surface failing calls, diagnose them, and iterate, not just a dashboard of call volume.


## The 8 Best Conversational AI Platforms for Retail Banking


### 1. Plivo


Best For: Regulated retail banks and mid-market financial institutions that need voice AI agents across multiple countries and channels


#### What It Does


Plivo is a 14-year communications infrastructure company with an owned carrier network in 150+ countries. It built a native voice AI agent layer into the telephony infrastructure itself, so the AI agent runtime, audio path, and telephony layer are one system. This matters for retail banking because the compliance chain-of-custody runs through a single vendor, and the call path has one hop instead of two or three.


Non-technical team members (contact center managers, compliance officers, branch ops leads) create and modify agents in plain English using the no-code studio. Developers get full control through the programmable API. Both build on the same platform, so a bank can start with no-code prototypes and graduate to API-driven agents without switching vendors.


For retail banking workflows that span channels, Plivo agents work across voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and chat with shared context. A customer calls about a disputed charge, gets it resolved, receives an SMS confirmation, and messages on WhatsApp two days later with a follow-up. The agent knows the full history across all three touchpoints.


#### Key Features


-


Owned carrier network in 150+ countries with one-hop call routing and 99.99% uptime SLA


-


Sub-500ms end-to-end latency with a 700–900ms optimal response window for natural-sounding pacing


-


HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2, PCI DSS, CSA STAR certifications with data residency in US, EU, and APAC


-


AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS in transit, full audit logs, and role-based access control


-


No-code studio for building agents in plain English, plus programmable API (Python, Node, Go, REST)


-


Omnichannel agents: voice, SMS, WhatsApp, and chat with shared context


-


Automated simulation testing against edge cases before production deployment


-


Per-call evaluation scoring against defined goals with a self-improvement loop


-


Bring-your-own-TTS architecture (including ElevenLabs voices) for premium voice quality on owned infrastructure


-


Turn detection, noise cancellation, and prosody tuning built into the default voice stack


-


Function calling and tool use mid-conversation (account lookups, balance checks, appointment booking)


-


Enterprise customer base includes Meta, Uber, Atlassian, and Adobe


#### Limitations


-


Agency white-label program with client management dashboards and volume pricing is not publicly available. Banks working with third-party integrators or agencies may find fewer structured partner tools compared to agency-focused platforms like Synthflow.


-


Pre-built integration catalog is narrower than Twilio's. Banks with complex multi-vendor software stacks should evaluate connector availability during procurement.


#### Pricing


Calls start at $0.004/min on Plivo's voice network. The AI Agents platform (including the Vibe Agent builder, simulation testing, concurrent calls, and knowledge base) is available on the Enterprise plan starting at $1,000/month. New accounts get $10 in free credits with no credit card required.


### 2. Twilio


Best For: Retail banks already deeply embedded in Twilio with existing contracts, approved vendor status, and Flex contact center dependencies


#### What It Does


Twilio is the default communication platform for developers: 15+ years of trust, publicly traded, $4B+ annual revenue. Its pitch for voice AI in banking is straightforward: "You already use Twilio. Now add AI." Products include Voice Intelligence, AI Assistants, and LLM integrations layered on top of the existing telephony stack.


For banks already running Twilio Flex for their contact center, the switching cost to a new platform is real. Twilio's pre-built integration catalog, the largest in this set, covers CRM, support, analytics, and data platforms. Its Flex product has mature human-to-AI handoff with queue management, skills-based routing, and supervisor tools that banking contact centers rely on.


#### Key Features


-


Largest telephony network in CPaaS with phone numbers in 100+ countries


-


SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, ISO 27001 certifications


-


Deep pre-built integration catalog with hundreds of connectors across CRM, support, and analytics categories


-


Flex contact center with mature human-to-AI handoff, queue management, and skills-based routing


-


Large developer community with extensive documentation, tutorials, and marketplace


-


Financial stability and existing enterprise contracts that banking procurement teams recognize


#### Limitations


-


AI is bolted on, not integrated. Building a voice AI agent means stitching together Twilio Voice, a separate speech-to-text integration, an LLM integration, a text-to-speech integration, and custom orchestration code. This adds development time and latency.


-


Twilio's internal ConversationRelay benchmark reports 491ms p50 and 713ms p95, but the published result doesn't fully define the inclusion of the customer application, model path, or network frames.


#### Pricing


Voice starts at ~$0.013–$0.022/min. Phone numbers cost $1–$2/month. AI features are charged separately. SMS runs $0.0079/segment. Total voice AI agent cost: ~$0.15–$0.25/min all-in. Paid support starts at $250/month.


### 3. ElevenLabs


Best For: Banks where voice quality is the top priority and everything else is secondary, or banks that want premium voices on another platform's infrastructure


#### What It Does


ElevenLabs is the leader in AI voice technology: text-to-speech with natural prosody, emotional range, and breathing patterns that no other provider in this set matches. It now offers ElevenAgents for real-time voice agents using ElevenLabs voices. The argument is that voice quality is the most important factor in customer experience, and ElevenLabs has the best voices.


For retail banking, voice quality matters. A customer calling about a stolen card needs to hear a voice that sounds calm, professional, and human. But voice quality alone doesn't make a banking platform. ElevenLabs doesn't own a carrier network, doesn't provision phone numbers, and doesn't handle call routing or failover. Its telephony compliance story covers the TTS product but not the full call path.


The practical move for banking: use ElevenLabs voices on Plivo. Plivo's bring-your-own-TTS architecture lets you run ElevenLabs voices on an owned carrier network with banking-grade compliance and omnichannel support. Same voice, different foundation.


#### Key Features


-


Voice quality with natural prosody, emotional range, pausing, and breathing patterns unmatched by other providers in this set


-


Voice cloning from short audio samples for custom brand voices


-


29+ languages with natural-sounding accents


-


ElevenAgents platform for deploying conversational voice agents


-


SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, PCI DSS Level 1, GDPR certifications


-


HIPAA available on Enterprise plans with signed BAA and Zero Retention Mode


-


Documented TTS API with code samples, SDKs, and integration guides


#### Limitations


-


No owned carrier network. No phone number provisioning, call routing, or carrier-grade failover. Conversational AI connects to phones through third-party carriers.


-


End-to-end phone call latency (including STT, LLM, and telephony) measured 1,424ms median in an independent benchmark, despite the TTS layer alone achieving ~75ms.


#### Pricing


ElevenAgents plans range from Free (15 min/mo) to Business ($990/mo, 12,375 min/mo). Additional minutes cost $0.08/min (standard) or $0.16/min (burst, over concurrency limit). Enterprise pricing is custom. LLM costs are currently absorbed by ElevenLabs but will eventually be passed through. TTS-only API usage is billed separately per character.


### 4. Vapi


Best For: Developer teams at banks or fintechs building custom voice AI products with no immediate compliance constraints


#### What It Does


Vapi is developer infrastructure for voice AI. It's a modular orchestration layer: pick your LLM, speech-to-text, and text-to-speech providers, wire them through Vapi, and build a voice agent via API. The modularity is genuine. You can swap any component without rewriting the agent. The developer community is active and the iteration speed is fast.


For retail banking, Vapi's limitation is structural. It doesn't own a telephony network. Every call routes through Vapi's layer plus a third-party carrier, adding latency and a second failure point. HIPAA requires an Enterprise plan or a $2,000/month add-on that[disables call logs and transcription review](https://www.greetmate.ai/blog/best-hipaa-compliant-voice-ai-agents-2026) . Banking teams that need compliance across the full call path will need to chain Vapi's SOC 2 to their carrier's SOC 2, which adds procurement complexity.


#### Key Features


-


Highly modular: swap any component (LLM, STT, TTS) without rewriting the agent


-


Active developer community with GitHub repos and Discord


-


Documentation with code samples in Python, Node.js, Go, and REST


-


Function calling (tool use mid-conversation) works well for account lookups and booking


-


SOC 2 Type II certified; HIPAA available as $2,000/mo add-on or on Enterprise plan


-


Transparent usage-based pricing with a free tier


-


Fast iteration speed with weekly feature releases


#### Limitations


-


No owned telephony. Independent[Tested Media benchmark](https://telnyx.com/resources/voice-ai-agents-compared-latency) measured 720ms median and 1,050ms p95 across 500 production calls.


-


API-only. No no-code builder. Banking ops teams can't build or modify agents without developers.


Pricing


$0.05–$0.07/min orchestration fee, plus pass-through costs for STT, LLM, and TTS providers. Total per-minute cost typically lands at $0.08–$0.15/min for production agents. Free tier with limited monthly minutes.


### 5. Retell AI


Best For: Mid-market banks wanting a visual builder plus API without committing to a full enterprise platform


#### What It Does


Retell AI splits the difference between API-first complexity and no-code simplicity. It offers a visual builder for semi-technical users and an API for developers, with a growing template library for common use cases like appointment booking and lead qualification. For mid-market banks with limited engineering staff, the dual interface is appealing.


Retell AI holds SOC 2 Type I and II certification and offers HIPAA compliance with a[self-serve BAA at no extra fee](https://docs.retellai.com/general/compliance) , which is a meaningful advantage over Vapi's $2,000/mo add-on. But it doesn't own a telephony network. Phone numbers are concentrated in the US with limited international availability. Banks operating across borders will hit coverage limits quickly.


#### Key Features


-


Dual interface: visual builder for business users, API for developers


-


Growing template library for appointment booking, lead qualification, and common service flows


-


SOC 2 Type I and II certified; HIPAA with self-serve BAA at no extra fee; GDPR with DPA and EU SCCs


-


Supports ElevenLabs and Retell's own voice models, among other TTS providers


-


Free tier with limited minutes for evaluation


#### Limitations


-


No owned telephony. Third-party carriers only. Phone numbers concentrated in the US.


-


Sub-800ms latency claim is nearly double Plivo's sub-500ms. The 300ms gap is perceptible during fast-paced banking conversations.


#### Pricing


$0.07–$0.12/min. Lower-cost configurations use Retell's own voices. ElevenLabs-powered agents cost more. Free tier with limited minutes.


### 6. Bland AI


Best For: Banks running high-volume outbound campaigns (payment reminders, collections, appointment confirmations) in the US


#### What It Does


Bland AI is built for AI phone calls at scale, outbound-first. Upload a contact list, configure a script, launch thousands of concurrent calls. It targets sales teams, collections agencies, and appointment-heavy operations. For retail banking, the outbound use case is real: payment reminders, collections calls, appointment confirmations, and satisfaction surveys run at high volume with relatively simple scripts.


Bland AI now holds SOC 2 Type I and II, HIPAA, GDPR, and PCI DSS 4.0.1 certifications. But it doesn't own its telephony, is primarily US-focused, and its voice quality is noticeably AI. For a bank where the phone call represents the brand, that voice quality gap matters.


#### Key Features


-


Outbound campaign product: upload a list, configure a script, launch thousands of concurrent calls


-


Pre-built CRM integrations with automatic outcome syncing


-


SOC 2 Type I and II, HIPAA, GDPR, PCI DSS 4.0.1 certifications


-


High concurrency for large contact lists


-


Dashboard with call volume, success rates, duration tracking, and AI sentiment analysis on transcripts


-


Aggressive pricing designed to undercut human call center costs


#### Limitations


-


Voice quality gap. Agents sound functional but noticeably AI. For banking brand experience, this can be disqualifying.


-


Homepage claims 400ms latency but doesn't disclose methodology. Independent benchmark measured 850ms median and 1,180ms p95.


#### Pricing


$0.07–$0.09/min. Trial credits available.


### 7. Synthflow AI


Best For: Community banks and credit unions that need a simple voice agent deployed fast with no engineering staff


#### What It Does


Synthflow AI is a fully no-code voice AI platform for non-technical users. Pick a template, customize it, deploy. A non-technical person can have an agent answering calls in an afternoon. The template library covers common use cases: appointment booking, after-hours answering, and basic account inquiry routing.


For community banks and credit unions with no dedicated AI engineering team, Synthflow's barrier to entry is the lowest in this set. It also has a strong agency channel with white-labeling and client management dashboards, which matters for community banks working with technology consultants.


Synthflow now lists SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, and ISO 27001 compliance on its[public pages](https://synthflow.ai/blog/hipaa-compliant-ai-agents) . Buyers with strict regulatory requirements should request current audit documentation directly.


#### Key Features


-


Fully no-code: deploy an agent in an afternoon without engineering staff


-


Large template library for appointment booking, after-hours answering, and basic inquiry routing


-


Agency-friendly: white-labeling, client management dashboards, volume pricing


-


Lists SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GDPR, and ISO 27001 on public compliance pages


-


Active community of builders sharing templates and best practices


-


Low barrier to entry with a free tier


#### Limitations


-


Ceiling on complexity. Multi-step tool calls, conditional branching on account type, and complex identity verification logic break the builder.


-


Community forums report latency spikes and dropped calls during peak usage.


-


No developer API escape hatch. Banks that outgrow templates must migrate to a different platform entirely.


#### Pricing


Tiered plans starting at ~$29–$49/month with per-minute charges beyond included minutes. Agency plans with white-labeling priced higher.


### 8. LiveKit


Best For: Banks building multimodal experiences that combine voice with video banking, screen sharing, or cobrowsing


#### What It Does


LiveKit is open-source real-time infrastructure for audio, video, and data. Voice AI agents are one use case on a general-purpose media platform. It's Apache 2.0 licensed, so developers can inspect, modify, and self-host everything.


For retail banking, LiveKit's genuine sweet spot is video banking: a customer opens a video call with a relationship manager, shares their screen to walk through a mortgage application, and gets real-time voice AI assistance during the conversation. No other platform in this set handles voice + video + screen sharing in one framework.


But LiveKit doesn't handle phone calls. It's WebRTC only (browser-to-browser, app-to-app). Connecting to the phone network requires a separate telephony provider, which adds latency, complexity, and another vendor to manage. For banks where the primary channel is phone calls, LiveKit alone isn't enough.


#### Key Features


-


Sub-100ms media transport latency for the audio path alone (fastest raw audio in this set)


-


Open-source core: inspect, modify, and self-host


-


Multimodal: voice, video, screen sharing, and data channels in one framework


-


Agents framework (Python SDK) with plugins for popular STT, LLM, and TTS providers


-


Self-hosting option for banks with strict data residency requirements


#### Limitations


-


No telephony. Does not handle phone calls. Connecting to the PSTN requires a separate provider.


-


No phone numbers. Can't provision numbers, route calls, handle caller ID, forwarding, or voicemail.


#### Pricing


LiveKit Cloud: ~$0.004/participant-minute for audio. Self-hosted: free (open-source), but the bank bears infrastructure costs. Total cost for voice AI agents is hard to predict because it includes LiveKit fees + telephony provider + STT/LLM/TTS providers.


## Choosing the Right Platform


The right choice depends on your bank's regulatory posture, existing vendor commitments, engineering capacity, and channel volume.


-


Full call-path compliance, multi-country: Plivo or Twilio — both own their telephony networks. Plivo's AI is native to the stack (lower latency, simpler, cheaper per-minute); Twilio's is bolted on top. If you're already deep in Twilio Flex, factor in real switching costs.


-


Custom voice product, compliance not urgent: Vapi — most modular API, strong docs/community, swappable components. Tradeoffs: no owned telephony, no no-code builder, HIPAA mode disables call logs.


-


No engineering staff (community bank/credit union): Synthflow AI — live in an afternoon, but low ceiling; migrate to something like Plivo once you need complex identity verification or multi-step workflows.


-


Voice quality is the priority: Plivo supports bring-your-own-TTS, so you can run ElevenLabs voices on Plivo's compliant carrier network — same voice, stronger foundation.


-


Exploring video banking (mortgage consults, cobrowsing): pair LiveKit (multimodal layer) with a telephony provider like Plivo.


-


High-volume US outbound (collections, reminders): Bland AI is cheaper, but test voice quality if brand reputation is on the line.


## The Verdict


For retail banks evaluating conversational AI in 2026, the shortlist gets small once you filter for owned telephony, full-path compliance, and omnichannel context. Plivo is the only platform in this set where the AI agent, the carrier network, and the compliance stack are one system. That single-vendor architecture is what makes it possible to run a voice agent that also sends the SMS confirmation and picks up the WhatsApp follow-up, all on one audit trail. The fastest way to test whether that architecture holds up for your bank is on your own call data.
